target_customer: Consumer web and app companies that need to stop account takeovers, bots and fake accounts
problem: Credential stuffing and stolen passwords lead to account takeovers that sites detect late. Castle adds behavior based risk scoring through a JavaScript snippet and API.
business_model: B2B SaaS API priced on usage
product_category: Account takeover and bot protection, fraud prevention

founders.name: Johan Brissmyr
previous_startups: SettleBox (earlier payments startup, outcome not stated)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch spells his first name Johann and says Castle grew out of SettleBox.

founders.name: Sebastian Wallin
founders.background_notes: Castle's blog says he and the CEO created Castle in 2015; other directories call him chief architect.

competitors.name: Kount
competitors.traction_then: Named by the CEO as a competitor in the March 2016 launch coverage

technical_complexity.rationale: Behavioral risk scoring from login and device signals, Tor and IP blacklists and a drop-in JavaScript snippet are standard but need good data and low latency.

defensibility.rationale: Customer event data and integration into login flows create some lock-in, but TechCrunch notes large vendors and enterprise tools already compete.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch quoted the CEO expecting big web services not to focus on this space as intensely. No incumbent acquisition found; Castle remains independent and active.

market_need_then: The March 2016 TechCrunch piece frames account takeover as a growing problem for consumer sites. Castle's own 2019 post says Series A funds growth, and the customer list now includes Atlassian, Canva and Rakuten. No hard 2016 spend data was found.

branding.domain_note: Uses castle.io; other Castle named companies exist (an alarm firm, castled.io).

brand_strength.rationale: Castle is a quiet B2B security brand; search found no press on the brand and name confusion with other companies called Castle.

outcome_analysis: Castle raised a 2 million dollar seed in November 2016 and a 9.2 million dollar Series A in February 2019 led by Index Ventures, and is still operating with enterprise customers and a new research team. Growth appears steady and capital efficient, with no acquisition or layoffs found. Revenue and headcount history were not found, so the strength of product market fit is inferred from its customer list.
notes: Funding figures for both rounds were read from search snippets of eWeek, Xconomy, VentureBeat and Castle's own blog; the eWeek and VentureBeat pages were not opened (eWeek fetch returned 403). Aggregators total 11.2 to 13.7 million raised. The YC directory lists Winter 2016 while TechCrunch says Spring 2016. Co-founder Sebastian Wallin is listed by the YC page. A directory claims acquisition by Pernod Ricard, which is a different company and ignored.
